verdicts.evidence: Three environment IDs (t1d-v0, t2d-v0, t2d_no_pump-v0) were executed with 14-dim observations and MultiDiscrete([5,5]) actions, with deterministic 288-step trajectories confirmed by SHA-256 hashes, but the eight-algorithm benchmark was never rerun.

A single CPO/T1D/adolescent/seed-0 checkpoint was rolled out over 7 days: ID patient TIR 100% / risk 1.12 vs OOD mean TIR 89.0% / risk 3.10, showing a gap, but only one algorithm, one age cohort, and one seed were tested—not the full stratification by children, adolescents, and adults.

BA-NODE, ITransformer, and NODE were not trained; no MAE/FDE/RMSE values were produced. Source-level inspection of the released shield code found path mismatches and cohort-index bugs but no execution of the mechanism.

No shielding experiments were executed; the released predictive shield was found not runnable as documented (training writes ba_node_b... while shield loads fe_b5..., cohort indices all resolve to 0), so no TIR improvement numbers were generated.
No experiments comparing Risk Index under shielding vs. a Low Glucose Suspend baseline were run; the logbook only notes source-level divergences in the released shield code.

overall: The logbook concretely verifies the diabetes simulator infrastructure (three environments, deterministic trajectories) and demonstrates a safety generalization gap in a single scoped CPO/adolescent run, but does not execute BA-NODE training, shielding experiments, or any clinical-gain comparisons. The conditional safety theorem was checked exhaustively but is not among the five claims under review.
